Here is a sample Semgrep rule in YAML format for the vulnerable and patched functions:

```yaml
---
id: vuln-dectalk-tts-3600d8ac
title: "Potential HTTP to HTTPS upgrade"
description: "The function uses http:// URL instead of https://, which may be a security issue."
severity: WARNING
languages:
  - typescript
metadata:
  tags:
    - network
  confidence: high
  falsePositivePercentage: low
  message: "This rule identifies potential HTTP to HTTPS upgrade vulnerabilities in TypeScript code."
pattern:
  - '(import { URL, URLSearchParams } from \'node:url\';)?\\s*export default async function dectalk(text: string): Promise<Buffer> {\\s*const url = new URL(\'http://tts.cyzon.us/tts\');\\s*url.search = new URLSearchParams({ text }).toString();\\s*const response = await fetch(url);\\s*if (!response.ok) {\\s*throw new Error(`${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);\\s*}'
  - '(import { Buffer } from \'node:buffer\';)?\\s*return Buffer.from(binaryData);}'
```

This rule will match the vulnerable function and throw a warning if it is detected. The pattern includes both the vulnerable code and the patched code to avoid matching the patched behavior. The id, severity, languages, and metadata fields are filled out as per the problem statement.
